correctness.rationale: The cylinder weights are compatible by summing a finite geometric progression and are units. Grouping the rational geometric moments by residues modulo 29^e gives the same weights; terms involving the difference between an integer and its residue contain 29^e with only unit denominators at 1/2. On the unit branches, the Taylor coefficient of degree j contains log(x^28)^j/j!, so coefficients of degrees j≥2 are divisible by 29^2, and for j≥3 by 29^3. The 28 finite differences and all fibers through k=3 were replayed by inclusion–exclusion power sums, independently of the frozen Stirling recurrence. The 27 normalized regular branches reduce to affine maps with unit slope and restricted analytic coefficients, so the error in a difference gains another digit and every output digit lifts uniquely. The unique critical branch has (G(t)−G(0))/29^2 congruent to 4t+9 binomial(t,2), so its derivative has the one simple root 21 mod 29. Expanding about its Hensel lift factors out (t−xi)^2; the residual unit after dividing by H''(xi)/2 is 1 modulo 29 as a restricted power series. Its analytic square root gives a congruence-preserving bijection after multiplication by t−xi. The replay confirms center 20672 mod 29^3 and leading quadratic unit 9/2=19 mod 29. For n≥k the nonunit integral vanishes modulo 29^k; every branch contributes one full set of t mod 29^(k−1) in an index period. This yields the stated square-root factor 29 at k≥2, including k=2, and a single preimage in residue 24 at k=1. Counting unit squares after removing even valuations yields the sum S_m and the stated Haar measure.
residual_risks: Read the square-root formula as k≥2; the lone residue 24 has one preimage in the mod-29 period. The tail image closure is the closure of arbitrarily late values, not a claim about extra early values.
The frozen script checks singular support and regular multiplicities through k=3, not every singular multiplicity individually; the independent replay compares every multiplicity at those levels.

evidence: The weighted congruence makes a finite branch computation possible, and the 3-adic record supplies analogous unit branches. The 19-adic Fibonacci record is a true quadratic-square-branch analogue for a different sequence.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The congruence alone does not identify the 27 regular rows or the singular slope and curvature. Even after computation, the all-level law needs a Morse-coordinate argument; it is not a specialization of the law at 3 or the Fibonacci case.

originality.rationale: Neither periodicity nor the weighted-moment method is new. The distinct result is the exact eventual 29-adic value set, including the one singular quadratic branch, Haar measure and multiplicities at every depth.
residual_risks: The Diagana–Maïga full text was unavailable and may have stronger interpolation results. Unindexed prime-specific calculations cannot be excluded. No priority is asserted for the period or the general p-adic methods.

value.rationale: The actual output distribution at a prime with both regular and quadratic lifting is a natural invariant of a classical sequence. The classification explains incomplete lifting in exactly one residue and gives both the limiting size and per-level occupancies, beyond finite modular data or a new proof of an old period.
residual_risks: The result makes no all-primes classification or claim of priority for being the smallest odd prime with a singular branch.
